question: True or false: people from every culture tested are fooled equally by two equal lines with arrow-shaped ends?
answer: False. In the 1960s Segall and colleagues tested people in more than a dozen societies. Students in Evanston, Illinois, saw the lines as most unequal; San foragers in the Kalahari were barely fooled at all. Why is still argued, perhaps a life among straight walls and corners. Textbooks had treated students' eyes as everyone's.
move: Ask who was tested before calling a finding human nature.
ask: Which of my everyone-thinks-this beliefs rests only on people like me?
trap: True, since an illusion seems built into the eye itself.
reference: Segall, Campbell & Herskovits, The Influence of Culture on Visual Perception, Bobbs-Merrill, 1966
